newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus president congratulates Britain's Blair.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus president congratulates Britain's Blair.

text.p: Cyprus on Friday congratulated British Prime Minister Tony Blair on his election win, expressing hopes he will press on with efforts to find a settlement to the division of the former British colony.

"We are confident that the Labour Party's declared positions on Cyprus will be effectively promoted," Glafcos Clerides, president of the eastern Mediterranean island that was a British colony between 1878 and 1960, said in a telegram to Blair.

"In this respect we trust that you personally and your government will pursue further the efforts for a just and viable solution to the long-standing Cyprus problem and the accession of Cyprus to the European Union," added Clerides, a British-trained barrister and RAF fighter pilot in the World War Two.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 after the military rulers of Greece engineered a coup in the capital Nicosia which toppled the legitimate government.
United Nations attempts to reunite the island's Greeks and Turks under a federal umbrella have failed.
Britain, Greece and Turkey are guarantor powers of Cyprus's sovereignty under international treaties.
Briatin's former Conservative government appointed Sir David Hannay, its former ambassador to the United Nations, as its special representative on the Cyprus issue last year.
